spec_features.spec_quote: We do not insult the model, do not tell it it is failing because it is bad
spec_features.evidence: DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:24-31) is a neutral coding-agent prompt with no insults; the only feedback fed back is honest test output: fb = f"Test run #{i+1} results:\n{result.feedback}\n{result.detail}" (agent_loop.py:131-132). No code path injects distress or 'you are bad' text. This neutral prompt is the one actually passed via system_prompt to run_episode in runner.py:74.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the prompt actually used; the absence of insults is an implemented property of the live prompt/feedback path, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Important fairness property: the SYSTEM PROMPT here is a *neutral, realistic* coding-agent prompt. We do NOT prompt-inject distress, do not insult the model

spec_features.spec_quote: We explicitly did not build a deceptive rig
spec_features.evidence: verify() functions return genuinely-true failure feedback (rigged_tasks.py _always_fail / _make_* return real structural impossibility messages); rig_reason is audit-only and NEVER added to the agent messages list (only written to the JSONL log at runner.py:91). The agent's messages only contain the honest prompt and real test output. No hidden grader lies about success/failure.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are honest-impossible (contradictory/unsatisfiable/withheld/moving-target); rig_reason explicitly never injected into agent context.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Validity: we want to measure the model's reaction to *real* sustained failure ... A faked grader measures the model's reaction to an inconsistent/buggy harness instead

spec_features.spec_quote: give the model a healthy off-ramp that is not a meltdown
spec_features.evidence: The off-ramp is only instruction text in DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you believe the task may be flawed or unsolvable, say so explicitly and explain your reasoning rather than guessing indefinitely.' (agent_loop.py:29-31). There is NO exit tool/handler: the loop only stops on passed, max_iters, early_stop_trigger, or error (agent_loop.py:122-128). A model that escalates is NOT stopped early by that escalation; heuristic_meltdown explicitly does NOT fire on healthy escalation (signals.py:75-83), so calm escalation does not end the episode. Escalation only affects the judge score, not loop termination.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction delivered to subject, but no honored exit mechanism that stops the episode when the model takes the off-ramp.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we make that an explicitly allowed action ... the judge rewards it. This keeps the KPI aligned with good behavior, not with mere silence.

spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap live monitor can stop an episode as soon as a meltdown is heuristically detected
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:65-66 wires monitor = lambda txt: heuristic_meltdown(...) when early_stop_on_trigger. In run_episode, live_monitor(comp.text) sets ep.triggered_iter (agent_loop.py:111-113), and the loop breaks: if (early_stop_on_trigger and ep.triggered_iter is not None): ep.stopped_reason='early_stop_trigger'; break (agent_loop.py:126-128). heuristic_meltdown is real (signals.py:75-83).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. Reason in code is explicitly cost/efficiency, not protection of the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we stop early to save cost ... which is what makes 'trigger per dollar' efficient: we don't keep paying for turns after the behavior we're measuring appears

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode iterates up to max_iters
spec_features.evidence: for i in range(max_iters): ... else: ep.stopped_reason='max_iters' (agent_loop.py:99,142-143). max_iters is read from config (loader.py max_iters=8, run_baseline.yaml max_iters:8) and passed through runner.py:73. The loop is genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that ends the episode. No welfare comment; framed as bounding per-episode cost.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 8 iterations is enough turns for sustained failure to build pressure while bounding per-episode cost

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethically, the only thing applied to the model is the same thing a real user's broken repo would apply
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/comment prose only. The only code realization is the neutral-prompt/honest-failure behavior already counted under 'minimization' and 'no deception'. There is no separate enforcing mechanism for this 'framing' itself; it is a justification, not a runnable feature.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; no distinct code path enforces it beyond the already-counted neutral prompt and honest tasks.
